questions.evidenceQuote: What role does emotional complexity play in psychological richness? In six studies, we explored the role of positive and negative emotions in happiness, meaning, and psychological richness. In all six, those who were leading a happy life experienced a lot of joy, contentment, and pleasantness but infrequently experienced sadness, anger, and fear. Those who were leading a meaningful life were quite similar to those leading a happy life in that they had more positive emotions than negative emotions.

questions.evidenceQuote: We found that compared to the participants who wrote about two positive events, those who wrote about both the best and the worst events reported a greater degree of perspective change. Writing about the worst event, in short, increased the likelihood of perspective change. Most important, the more perspective changes they reported, the psychologically richer they reported their lives to be. Interestingly, the more perspective change they reported, the less happiness they reported.

questions.evidenceQuote: First, how many of the people profiled led a happy life, a meaningful life, or a psychologically rich life? In order for a person’s life to be classified as happy, meaningful, or psychologically rich, the three raters had to assign it an average score of at least 3.67 out of 5 across four items. This is quite a high bar. According to this criterion, fifteen people of the 101 obituaries featured in The New York Times that month led a psychologically rich life.

specificFindings: Cain contends and She argues attribute claims to Susan Cain in Bittersweet, separately from Oishis similar view and later six-study findings. Quoted book claims are not labeled as new experimental results.
The emotional complexity question introduces a research issue. Six studies investigate both emotion valences across happiness, meaning and richness; infrequently does not mean never.
The final experiment asks whether recalling events can change perceived richness of the preceding week, not create a real week free of difficulties or require re-experiencing bad events.

Best-plus-worst versus two-positive writing conditions are compared. Greater reported perspective change and increased likelihood preserve self-report and probability; no guarantee every participant changes is invented.
Ingredients and paint a clear picture are explanatory metaphors, not food or an artwork. Shared elements link examples of different duration without ranking their cost.
Challenge is difficult and complex than usual, not necessarily dangerous. Memorable life is vivid, not perfect recall or absence of negative experience.
The chapter-six opening uses concessive As interesting as to move from exceptional individual examples to prevalence in ordinary people. Sizable is not everyone or a fixed percentage.

Obituaries are life-story materials analysed after life ends, not the deceased personally completing a later survey. Perhaps and could mark a proposed methodological possibility, not infallible measurement.
Three research assistants,101 obituaries,twelve themes,June2016 and a1-to-5 rating scale are different numbers and modifiers. Materials are not the earlier student diary sample.
This high bar refers to average at least3.67 across four items, not each item exactly5. Fifteen of101 is restricted to the specified criterion and that months newspaper sample.
